records.description: Illustrierter Film-Kurier Nr. 1499 — film programme for Alraune (Germany, 1930), directed by Richard Oswald, with music by Bronisław Kaper. records.title: Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung, 10 December 1929 — Jazz auf vier Flügeln review
records.publicCaption: Review titled “Jazz auf vier Flügeln,” published in Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung on 10 December 1929, documenting the First Piano Quartet with Bronisław Kaper, Leopold Mittmann, Alexander Zakin and Julian Pomeranc.
records.description: Review titled ‘Jazz auf vier Flügeln — Zweites städtisches Sonderkonzert in Hamborn’ (signed Dr. Funk) in the Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung, 10 December 1929. It covers the First Piano Quartet (Erstes Klavier-Quartett) of four pianists — Bronisław Kaper, Leopold Mittmann, Alexander Zakin and Julian Pomeranc — performing on four grand pianos, including their own compositions. The programme ranged from Schubert, Verdi, Strauss, Kreisler and Rimsky-Korsakov to the ‘Blue Danube’ and modern dances; Kaper contributed a tango for four grand pianos (Vierflügeltango), and Mittmann a Jazz-Prélude and three ‘Jazz-Babies’.

records.publicCaption: Georg Jacoby during the filming of Die geschiedene Frau in the Dutch bulb-growing region, 26 April 1953 — two decades after the work documented here. Jacoby directed Melodie der Liebe (1932), for which Kaper wrote music.

records.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the film director Georg Jacoby standing outdoors during filming, 1953.

records.title: Harold Adamson — portrait photograph
records.publicCaption: Harold Adamson, American lyricist. Adamson wrote the words for “Ninon” (1935), set to music by Kaper.
records.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified; via the Songwriters Hall of Fame and English Wikipedia.
records.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. A reduced-resolution reproduction (286 × 348 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
records.altText: Black-and-white portrait photograph of the lyricist Harold Adamson.

records.title: Robert Z. Leonard — portrait, 1926
records.publicCaption: Robert Z. Leonard, published in The Motion Picture Director in July 1926. Leonard directed Escapade (1935) and Maytime (1937), both documented here.
records.publicCreditLine: Artist unknown; The Motion Picture Director, July 1926, via the Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States: published in a magazine before 1 January 1931. The Wikimedia Commons file records the issue and links the Internet Archive scan, so the publication and its date are established rather than assumed.
records.altText: Black-and-white portrait photograph of the film director Robert Z. Leonard, 1926.

records.title: Anthony Asquith directing Channel Incident, September 1940
records.publicCaption: Anthony Asquith directing Peggy Ashcroft and Gordon Harker in Channel Incident, a Ministry of Information film about the evacuation of Dunkirk, September 1940. Asquith directed Moscow Nights (1935), for which Kaper wrote the music.
records.publicCreditLine: Ministry of Information Photo Division photographer; Imperial War Museums, D 1076A.
records.rightsNote: Crown copyright, expired: the photograph was taken before 1 June 1957, and HMSO has stated that the expiry of Crown copyright applies worldwide. Catalogued by the Imperial War Museums as created for the Ministry of Information, dissolved in 1946.
records.altText: Anthony Asquith directing actors aboard a motor yacht on a film set, September 1940.

records.title: Deanna Durbin — Cine Mundial cover portrait, February 1938
records.publicCaption: Deanna Durbin on the cover of Cine Mundial, February 1938 — a painted portrait by Jose M. Recoder, not a photograph. Durbin sang “My heart is singing” and “Someone to care for me”, written for her by Kaper and Jurmann for Three Smart Girls (1936).
records.publicCreditLine: Jose M. Recoder, Cine Mundial, February 1938, via the Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States: published between 1931 and 1963 with the copyright not renewed, per the Wikimedia Commons file, which cites the issue and links the Internet Archive scan. The Commons template notes the work may remain protected where the rule of the shorter term is not applied to United States works.
records.altText: Painted cover portrait of the singer Deanna Durbin by Jose M. Recoder, Cine Mundial, February 1938.

records.title: Judy Garland — publicity photograph, 1936
records.publicCaption: Judy Garland in a studio publicity photograph issued for Pigskin Parade (1936), her feature debut. The following year she sang “Swing, Mister Mendelssohn”, by Kaper and Jurmann, in Everybody Sing (MGM, 1938).
records.publicCreditLine: 20th Century Fox, via Heritage Auctions and Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States: published between 1931 and 1977 without a copyright notice, per the Wikimedia Commons file. Two details are recorded rather than smoothed over: the Heritage Auctions lot the file was taken from is described as an MGM group of the 1940s, while the uploader dates this print to 1936 and attributes it to 20th Century Fox, which matches Pigskin Parade; and the Commons copy has been digitally cleaned.
records.altText: Black-and-white publicity portrait of the young Judy Garland, 1936.

records.title: Jeanette MacDonald — studio portrait, 1930s
records.publicCaption: Jeanette MacDonald in an undated studio portrait of the 1930s. MacDonald introduced “San Francisco”, by Kaper and Jurmann with words by Gus Kahn, in the MGM film of 1936; the song carried the picture and outlived it.
records.publicCreditLine: Photographer unknown; via Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States: Wikimedia Commons records the photograph as published between 1931 and 1977 without a copyright notice and also applies a United Kingdom tag for anonymous works. The claim rests on the uploader’s inspection of the unmarked print rather than on an identified publication; the file cites only a photo-gallery web article, so the image’s provenance remains limited.
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of the singer and actress Jeanette MacDonald, 1930s.

records.title: Hans Albers in Berlin, 1924
records.publicCaption: Hans Albers photographed walking Unter den Linden in Berlin, 1924 — nine years before he took the lead in Heut’ kommt’s drauf an, the 1933 comedy for which Kaper and Jurmann wrote the songs.
records.publicCreditLine: Bundesarchiv, Bild 102-00586A / photographer unknown; CC BY-SA 3.0 DE.
records.rightsNote: Licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Germany by the Bundesarchiv, which supplied the Bild 102 series to Wikimedia Commons through a cooperation project. The file is a Wikimedia Commons crop from the original plate, which shows Albers with an unidentified Italian tenor.
records.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the actor Hans Albers in a coat and hat on a Berlin street, 1924.

records.title: Marc Lavry — portrait by Helmar Lerski, 1944
records.publicCaption: Marc Lavry photographed by Helmar Lerski in 1944, thirteen years after he directed the music for Seitensprünge (1931) in Berlin. Lavry conducted the Berliner Sinfonie Orchester from 1928 until the orchestra was dismantled under the National Socialist regime, and left for Riga in 1933.
records.publicCreditLine: Helmar Lerski, 1944; via the Marc Lavry Heritage Society and Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in Israel: the Wikimedia Commons file carries the PD-Israel tag, under which copyright in a photograph made before 2008 expires fifty years after it was taken, so the term ended in 1994. That ground is Israeli, not United States law; Lerski died in 1956, so the work remains protected until 2027 in countries applying a seventy-year term from the author’s death, and the United States position for a 1944 foreign photograph depends on restoration under the URAA. The photograph is dated 1944, well after the 1931 film documented here.
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of the composer and conductor Marc Lavry, photographed by Helmar Lerski in 1944.

records.title: Alfred Piccaver — portrait, Bain News Service
records.publicCaption: Alfred Piccaver, the English-born tenor who led the Vienna State Opera for a quarter of a century. He took the lead in Abenteuer am Lido (1933), the Austrian musical comedy scored by Kaper and Jurmann and his one substantial film role.
records.publicCreditLine: Unknown photographer, Bain News Service; Library of Congress, George Grantham Bain Collection, ggbain.34250.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States under the PD-US tag on the Wikimedia Commons file. The photograph comes from the Library of Congress George Grantham Bain Collection, for which the Library records no known restrictions on publication. Neither the photographer nor the exact date is established; the Commons file gives the date as unknown, and the collection’s Piccaver portraits are dated by the Library between 1910 and the 1920s.
records.altText: Black-and-white portrait photograph of the tenor Alfred Piccaver.

records.title: Albert Chantrier and René Nazelles — La Rampe, 1921
records.publicCaption: Albert Chantrier and René Nazelles, composer and lyricist of Le Fruit défendu, photographed for La Rampe on the operetta’s run at the Théâtre Cluny. Nazelles went on to write French lyrics for Kaper.
records.publicCreditLine: Unsigned photograph, La Rampe, 9 January 1921, p. 12; Bibliothèque nationale de France, Gallica, ark:/12148/bpt6k55821649.
records.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph appeared unsigned in a French periodical published on 9 January 1921 and is therefore an anonymous work, free in France seventy years after publication, that is from 1992. It was already in the public domain in its source country on the URAA date of 1 January 1996, so no United States copyright was restored, and a work published in 1921 is in any case out of copyright in the United States. Reproduced from the Bibliothèque nationale de France digitisation.
records.altText: Black-and-white press photograph of two men in hats and overcoats standing at a café table, reading a sheet of paper.

records.title: André de Badet — portrait, Gaîté-Lyrique programme, 1941
records.publicCaption: André de Badet, the librettist and lyricist who wrote French words for seven Kaper songs, in the author’s portrait printed in the programme of his operetta L’Auberge qui chante at the Gaîté-Lyrique.
records.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified, blindstamp partly legible as “…e STUDIO”; programme of L’Auberge qui chante, Gaîté-Lyrique, 4 October 1941. Bibliothèque nationale de France, Arts du spectacle, 8-RSUPP-879.
records.rightsNote: The 1941 programme is digitized by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, but neither the catalogue record nor the partly legible studio blindstamp identifies the photographer or supplies a licence for the underlying portrait. Copyright status cannot be determined from the available evidence.
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of André de Badet in jacket and tie, facing the camera.

records.title: René Pujol — portrait by Henri Manuel, 1932
records.publicCaption: René Pujol, the Bordeaux-born librettist who wrote with Charles-Louis Pothier under Albert Willemetz at the Bouffes-Parisiens, photographed by Henri Manuel for the programme of La Pouponnière.
records.publicCreditLine: Henri Manuel (1874–1947); programme of La Pouponnière, Bouffes-Parisiens, 1932, collection Jacques Gana, via the Encyclopédie de la comédie musicale.
records.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The photographer, Henri Manuel, died in 1947, so the French term expired on 1 January 2018; because the work was still protected in France on the URAA date of 1 January 1996, United States copyright was restored and runs ninety-five years from the 1932 publication, to 1 January 2028. The site that reproduces the programme grants no licence, stating that illustrations remain the copyright of their respective rightsholders. A reduced-resolution reproduction (700 × 852 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of René Pujol in profile, wearing a suit.

records.title: Henry Koster — Universal-International press photograph, 1961
records.publicCaption: Henry Koster, who directed Three Smart Girls in 1936, the Deanna Durbin debut that carried two songs by Kaper and Jurmann. The photograph is a later studio still, made for Flower Drum Song in 1961.
records.publicCreditLine: Universal-International, press photograph for Flower Drum Song, 1961; Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. The Wikimedia Commons file carries the PD-US-not-renewed tag: the photograph was published in the United States in 1961, within the 1931–1963 window in which copyright had to be renewed, and no renewal is recorded. The Commons file page notes that the image may remain protected in jurisdictions that do not apply the rule of the shorter term to United States works.
records.altText: Black-and-white press photograph of the film director Henry Koster.

records.title: Frank Lloyd with his Best Director award, April 1930
records.publicCaption: Frank Lloyd at the second Academy Awards ceremony on 3 April 1930, holding the Best Director award for The Divine Lady. Five years later he directed Mutiny on the Bounty, for which Kaper wrote “Love Song of Tahiti” with Walter Jurmann and Gus Kahn.
records.publicCreditLine: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, 3 April 1930; via Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. The photograph was published in 1930, so its ninety-five-year term expired on 1 January 2026; no question of renewal arises and the URAA does not apply to a United States work. The Wikimedia Commons file carries the PD-US-expired tag on the same reasoning.
records.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the film director Frank Lloyd in evening dress, holding an Academy Award statuette.

records.title: Charles-Louis Pothier — portrait, Flossie programme, 1929
records.publicCaption: Charles-Louis Pothier, the Bordeaux-born lyricist who worked with René Pujol as librettist-parolier to Albert Willemetz at the Bouffes-Parisiens, in the author’s portrait from the programme of Flossie.
records.publicCreditLine: Pierre Carles; programme of Flossie, Bouffes-Parisiens, 1929, collection Jacques Gana, via the Encyclopédie de la comédie musicale.
records.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The photograph is credited to Pierre Carles, but the photographer could not be traced: he holds no authority record or Wikidata item, appears in no Wikimedia Commons attribution, and is absent as a creator from the digitised holdings of the Bibliothèque nationale de France. Without a date of death the French term cannot be computed, and a French work published in 1929 would in any case have had United States copyright restored by the URAA if it was still protected in France in 1996. The site reproducing the programme grants no licence, stating that illustrations remain the copyright of their respective rightsholders. A reduced-resolution reproduction (700 × 594 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of Charles-Louis Pothier in a suit and tie.

records.title: United States–Mexico border crossing at Calexico, c. 1927
records.publicCaption: The Calexico–Mexicali crossing photographed for the Los Angeles Times about 1927. Kaper entered the United States here on 1 November 1935, eight years after this view was taken, so the picture shows the place rather than the day.
records.publicCreditLine: Los Angeles Times Photographic Collection, UCLA Library Special Collections, Charles E. Young Research Library; uclamss_1429_0385, ark:/21198/zz002d9ndg. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
records.rightsNote: Licensed for reuse. UCLA records the item as copyrighted, names itself as rights holder and licenses it under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, which permits reproduction with attribution; the credit line above carries that attribution. Had the photograph been published in 1927 it would in any case be public domain in the United States, the ninety-five-year term having expired in 2022, but UCLA links it to the July 1927 reports only as a possibility and does not confirm publication, so the licence rather than expiry is the basis relied on here.
records.altText: Bird’s-eye photograph of the United States–Mexico border crossing at Calexico, with two security booths, cars and pedestrians passing under a sign reading Mexico.

records.title: Château des Fleurs — opening advertisement, 1927
records.publicCaption: Château des Fleurs, Franklin Avenue at Cherokee Street, Hollywood. Opening advertisement, 10 August 1927.
records.description: Opening advertisement for the Hollywood apartment building documented as Bronisław Kaper’s residence in February 1936.
records.publicCreditLine: Los Angeles Times, 10 August 1927; reproduced by the City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States: the advertisement was published in 1927. The displayed image is a crop from the reproduction in an official City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning report.
records.altText: Black-and-white 1927 advertisement for Château des Fleurs, with an architectural drawing of the French Norman Revival apartment building above decorative text.

records.title: Hotel Comercial, Mexicali — historical postcard
records.publicCaption: Hotel Comercial in Mexicali, shown in an undated historical postcard. Kaper’s 1935 immigration manifest records this hotel as his last permanent residence abroad.
records.description: Historical postcard view explicitly captioned Hotel Comercial in Mexicali, the hotel recorded as Kaper’s last permanent residence abroad in his 1 November 1935 immigration manifest.
records.publicCreditLine: Historical postcard, photographer and publisher unidentified; México en Fotos, photo MX13895529520026, uploaded by centli.
records.rightsNote: Copyright status and the original photographer and publisher have not been identified. It does not substitute for a collectible or archival original; México en Fotos is credited and linked as the immediate source.
records.altText: Sepia postcard view of the arcaded Hotel Comercial in Mexicali, with palm trees and a water tower beside the building.

records.title: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Studios, Culver City — street view
records.publicCaption: Street view of the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer studio complex in Culver City, showing the studio buildings and rooftop MGM sign. Undated historical photograph.
records.description: Undated historical street view of the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer studio complex in Culver City, the studio associated with Kaper’s Hollywood career.
records.publicCreditLine: City of Culver City, Culver City Historic Images; photographer and date unidentified.
records.rightsNote: The City of Culver City’s historic-image page supplies this photograph without a date, photographer credit or reuse licence. Copyright status therefore remains undetermined. The 740 × 522 pixel image is reproduced without enlargement for non-commercial scholarly identification and discussion of the MGM studio site associated with Kaper’s Hollywood career. The City of Culver City is credited and linked as the immediate institutional source.
records.altText: Black-and-white street view of the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer studio complex in Culver City, with parked cars, a long colonnaded building and the MGM rooftop sign.

records.title: Edmund Goulding — Photoplay, December 1922
records.publicCaption: Edmund Goulding, who directed Maytime in 1937. The portrait is much earlier: it was printed in Photoplay in December 1922, when Goulding was working in Hollywood as a screenwriter.
records.publicCreditLine: Unknown photographer; Photoplay 22 (December 1922), p. 61, digitised at the Internet Archive; Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. The photograph was first published in Photoplay in December 1922, before 1 January 1931, so United States copyright has expired. The Wikimedia Commons file page notes that the image may still be protected outside the United States in jurisdictions that do not apply the rule of the shorter term to United States works. The photographer is not named in the magazine.
records.altText: Halftone head-and-shoulders portrait of the film director Edmund Goulding in a suit and tie.

records.title: Norman Hackforth — Royal Navy photograph, HMS Victorious, 1 August 1944
records.publicCaption: Norman Hackforth, who wrote the English lyric of “The Sweetest Song in All the World” in 1934, at the piano during Noël Coward’s concert for the men of the Eastern Fleet aboard HMS Victorious at Trincomalee, 1 August 1944. This detail is cropped from the Royal Navy photograph.
records.publicCreditLine: Royal Navy official photographer; Imperial War Museums, A 25390; Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was taken on 1 August 1944 by an official Royal Navy photographer and is Crown copyright. Crown copyright in photographs created before 1 June 1957 ran for fifty years from creation, so the image entered the public domain in the United Kingdom in 1995 and was therefore already free on the United States restoration date of 1 January 1996, which leaves it unrestored by the URAA. Reproduced from the cropped detail published on Wikimedia Commons; the full frame shows Coward at the microphone.
records.altText: Black-and-white photograph of Norman Hackforth playing an upright piano on a stage hung with Union flags.

records.title: Edwin L. Marin — Universal publicity still, Paris Calling, 1941 (detail)
records.publicCaption: Edwin L. Marin, who directed Man of the People in 1937 and Everybody Sing in 1938, photographed with a script on the set of Paris Calling in 1941. This detail is cropped to Marin from a Universal publicity still that also shows Elisabeth Bergner.
records.publicCreditLine: Unknown photographer (Universal Pictures), publicity still for Paris Calling, 1941; Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. Wikimedia Commons records the Universal Pictures publicity still as published without a copyright notice, placing it in the public domain on publication in 1941. The photographer is unidentified. The displayed 227 × 267 px detail is cropped to Marin from the 499 × 620 px still.
records.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the film director Edwin L. Marin holding a script, a cigarette in his hand.

records.title: Henri-Georges Clouzot — Studio Harcourt portrait, 1947
records.publicCaption: Henri-Georges Clouzot, credited as director of Tout pour l’amour in 1933. The portrait is later: Studio Harcourt photographed him in 1947, the year of Quai des Orfèvres.
records.publicCreditLine: Studio Harcourt, 1947; Réunion des musées nationaux; Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared, and the public-domain tag carried by the Wikimedia Commons file is not relied on here. The photograph was made by Studio Harcourt in 1947 and is distributed by the Réunion des musées nationaux, which licenses it commercially. As a French collective work its term runs seventy years from publication, so it was still protected in France on 1 January 1996, the United States restoration date, and the URAA therefore restored United States copyright for ninety-five years from publication. A reduced-resolution reproduction (360 × 489 px, from 479 × 650 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of Henri-Georges Clouzot in profile.

records.title: Joseph H. Lewis — on the set of The Undercover Man, 1949
records.publicCaption: Joseph H. Lewis, director of The Spy Ring (1938), photographed on the set of The Undercover Man in 1949. The Spy Ring is linked to Kaper only as probable stock-music context, not as a confirmed Kaper credit.
records.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified, on the set of The Undercover Man, 1949; via Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The Wikimedia Commons file carries a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0 licence attributed to a Flickr account, but a Flickr user cannot license a studio production still made in 1949, so that licence is not relied on here. The underlying photograph is a United States studio still from 1949, inside the 1931–1963 window in which copyright had to be renewed; no renewal has been checked, so its status is unverified rather than known to be free. A reduced-resolution reproduction (320 × 220 px, from 418 × 288 px) is used here for scholarly identification.
records.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the film director Joseph H. Lewis seated on a film set beside a camera.

records.title: Marcella Halicz — detail of the reception for Jan Kiepura, Paris, November 1933
records.publicCaption: Marcella Halicz, Jan Kiepura’s secretary and the author of the Polish lyrics of Ninon, ach uśmiechnij się! and Signorina, signorina, at the cocktail reception Kiepura gave in Paris in November 1933. Detail of the group photograph in which Kaper stands second from the left.
records.description: Identification follows the archival caption, which names the guests: Jan Kiepura fifth from the right, the Paris photographer Zygmunt Frenkiel first from the left, Bronisław Kaper second from the left, the director Ryszard Ordyński fifth from the left, the singer Adam Didur ninth from the right, the poet Jan Lechoń in the centre in spectacles, Kaper’s wife in the centre, and — among the women at the right edge — Kiepura’s secretary Marcella Halicz together with Alicja Brun, whom the caption distinguishes as the one holding a photograph of Kiepura. The woman shown in this detail stands beside the guest holding that photograph and is therefore Halicz. The detail was located in the full frame by correlation: it corresponds to a 315 × 466 px region of the 2035 × 2560 px scan and is reproduced here enlarged.
records.publicCreditLine: Narodowe Archiwum Cyfrowe, Koncern Ilustrowany Kurier Codzienny – Archiwum Ilustracji, ref. 3/1/0/11/8270/3; the frame was published in Światowid 46 (483), 11 November 1933.
records.rightsNote: Public domain. Narodowe Archiwum Cyfrowe records the object as public domain and permits reproduction, adaptation and distribution, including commercial use, without permission. The displayed 420 × 622 px detail is cropped from the 2035 × 2560 px scan of the separately catalogued group photograph.
records.altText: Detail of a 1933 press photograph showing Marcella Halicz in profile, wearing a pearl necklace.

records.title: Alexander Zakin — studio portrait by Max Dupain, July 1947
records.publicCaption: Alexander Zakin performed in the 1929 Vierflügeltango for four grand pianos and in the ERKLA-Quartett concert at Hamborn in December 1929, where he played alongside Kaper. Max Dupain made this later portrait in July 1947.
records.publicCreditLine: Max Dupain, July 1947; Mitchell Library, State Library of New South Wales, ON 558/Box 13/no. 90; via Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The Wikimedia Commons file carries only the Australian public-domain tag, which is correct for Australia — copyright in photographs taken before 1955 ran fifty years from creation, so this 1947 portrait became free there on 1 January 1998 — but the file makes no claim for the United States, and none can be made: because the photograph was still protected in Australia on 1 January 1996, the URAA restored its United States copyright. Max Dupain died in 1992. The holding library asks to be acknowledged. A reduced-resolution reproduction (500 × 674 px, from 3710 × 5000 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of the pianist Alexander Zakin.

records.title: Joseph Santley — Celebrated Actor Folks’ Cookeries, 1916
records.publicCaption: Joseph Santley, who directed We Went to College in 1936. The portrait is much earlier and shows him as a stage actor: it was printed in Celebrated Actor Folks’ Cookeries in 1916, two decades before he began directing in Hollywood.
records.publicCreditLine: Photographer unnamed; Celebrated Actor Folks’ Cookeries (New York: Mabel Rowland, Inc., 1916), p. 77; Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. The portrait was published in a United States book of 1916, before 1 January 1931, so United States copyright has expired. The book credits no photographer — the Wikimedia Commons author field names the publisher, Mabel Rowland, Inc. — so no term can be computed from a photographer’s death, and the image may remain protected in jurisdictions that do not apply the rule of the shorter term to United States works.
records.altText: Halftone portrait of the actor and director Joseph Santley in a suit.

records.title: Herbert Stothart — Picture Play, 1930 (detail)
records.publicCaption: Herbert Stothart, who scored Mutiny on the Bounty and A Night at the Opera in 1935 and San Francisco in 1936, going over a new song with Ramon Novarro for Devil May Care. Detail of a photograph printed in Picture Play in 1930, in a feature on the theme song at the coming of sound.
records.description: The printed caption reads: "Herbert Stothart, right, goes over a new song with Ramon Novarro, who sings several numbers in ‘Devil May Care.’" The caption reverses the two men. The figure on the right is identifiable as Ramon Novarro by comparison with his published portraits, so the composer is the man on the left, in shirtsleeves with the sheet music, and it is that figure which is reproduced here. The caption names only these two, which is what makes the identification safe.
records.publicCreditLine: Photographer unnamed; Picture Play Magazine, vol. 31–32 (January–June 1930), p. 97; digitised by the Media History Digital Library from the copy in the Museum of Modern Art Library, New York.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. The photograph was published in Picture Play Magazine in the first half of 1930, before 1 January 1931, so United States copyright has expired. No photographer is credited in the magazine. The image may remain protected in jurisdictions that do not apply the rule of the shorter term to United States works.
records.altText: Detail of a 1930 magazine photograph showing Herbert Stothart seated with sheet music.

records.title: Franz Waxman — Musical Courier, July 1955 (detail)
records.publicCaption: Franz Waxman, documented in connection with Trouble for Two (1936), A Day at the Races (1937) and The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1939), rehearses with Les Brown’s Band of Renown for the opening concert of the Los Angeles Music Festival in June 1955, which Waxman conducted.
records.description: The printed caption identifies the two men by what they are holding rather than by position: “FRANZ WAXMAN (with saxophone), music director and conductor of the 1955 Los Angeles Music Festival, rehearses with Les Brown for the opening night concert of the Festival on June 6. Waxman conducted Brown’s Band of Renown and the Festival Symphony Orchestra in the West Coast premiere of Liebermann’s Concerto for Jazz Band and Symphony Orchestra.” The reproduced detail shows the man holding the saxophone. The photograph is credited “Photo: Dave Pell.”
records.publicCreditLine: Photograph credited to Dave Pell; Musical Courier, vol. 152, no. 1 (July 1955), p. 27; Summy-Birchard Publishing Company; scanned copy at the Internet Archive.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. The photograph was published in Musical Courier in July 1955, when copyright required renewal after twenty-eight years. The Online Books Page inventory compiled from the Catalog of Copyright Entries and Copyright Office records lists May 1961 as the first renewed issue of the title, indicating that the 1955 issue copyright was not renewed and expired on 1 January 1984. The inventory notes that some individual contributions were renewed separately; no separate registration has been identified for this photograph, which carries only a caption credit. The displayed image is a 340 × 491 px detail cropped to Waxman.
records.altText: Detail of a 1955 magazine photograph showing Franz Waxman in glasses, playing a saxophone.

records.title: J. Walter Ruben — Who’s Who at Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, 1937
records.publicCaption: J. Walter Ruben, who directed Trouble for Two in 1936. The portrait accompanies his entry in the publicity reference book Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer issued in 1937.
records.description: Portrait detail cropped from the page carrying the entry “J. WALTER RUBEN” in the digitised book. The full page and its biographical text remain available in the linked scan.
